---- Applicant

 Sarkanda, District - Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh.

---- Respondent
For Applicant : Mr. Gautam Khetrapal, Advocate For State : Mr. Vinay Pandey, Dy. A.G.
For complainant : Mr. Rahul Pathak, Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu Order On Board 15/06/2024 1.
Heard.

2. Admit.
3.
Learned State counsel submits that case diary is available.
4. With the consent of both the parties, case is heard finally.
5. Applicant has filed this second bail application under Section 439 of CrPC for grant of regular bail.
First bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to repeat the prayer at appropriate stage.

6. Applicant was arrested in connection with Crime No. 207 of 2024 registered at Police Station Sarkanda, District - Bilaspur (C.G.) for offence punishable under Section 420 of I.P.C.
7.

Learned counsel for applicant submits that complainant has lodged a report against applicant alleging that applicant had fraudulently obtained Rs. 9,17,000/- for executing sale deed of a land in Pankaj Parasar Dubey vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5587627/
1 her favor.

sentences.text: However, upon inquiry, it was found that the land which was shown to complainant for selling it to her was owned by some other person.

After getting knowledge that applicant is not owner of the land which was shown to her by applicant, she made demand of amount of Rs.
9,17,000/- paid by her, however, it was not paid to her and therefore report was lodged.
It is contended that complainant had obtained Rs. 1,80,000/- from one Neeraj Soni for selling her land/house which has been paid by applicant and Rs. 80,000/- to Preeti Soni also.

After filing of bail application, applicant has paid Rs. 1,50,000/- and Rs. 4,00,000/- to complainant and thereby,
substantial amount has already been paid.
Applicant is in jail since 12.02.2024, offence is triable by Judicial Magistrate, charge- sheet has been filed, trial may take some time, hence, he may be enlarged on bail.

8. Learned State counsel and learned counsel for complainant opposes the submission made by learned counsel for applicant and submit that complainant is entitle for return of Rs. 9,17,000/,
however only Rs. 5,50,000/- has been returned by applicant.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

10. Taking into consideration facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation, period of detention of applicant, offence to be triable by Judicial Magistrate, without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.
11. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail, upon furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court on the conditions that - a) Applicant shall appear before the Trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
b) The applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c) If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd/-d/-
 (Parth Prateem Sahu)
